name: email-quoted-localpart-not-equal-invalid
description: permittedSubtrees rfc822Name is the complete mailbox 'foo@example.com'. The leaf SAN encodes the localpart in quoted-string form: '"foo"@example.com'. Per RFC 5321 and RFC 5322 the quoted-string and dot-atom local-part forms are distinct lexical productions; a validator that compares them as raw byte strings will reject them as unequal (correctly), but a validator that strips the quotes (or treats the quotes as significant in only one direction) may incorrectly match them. The leaf must be rejected — either because the local-parts are not byte-equal, or because the quoted form is unsupported syntax.
references: BoringSSL 1616d692 — crypto/x509 nc_email: sync to libpki's logic
notes: Constructed via unknown_extensions because cryptography's RFC822Name API normalises or rejects the leading quote.

BoringSSL post-fix rejects either side of this pair as UNSUPPORTED_NAME_SYNTAX since it doesn't support quoted local-parts at all. Implementations that strip quotes and compare 'foo' vs 'foo' (ignoring the structural difference) would incorrectly accept.
